Beginner.learningGoal: Write and call async methods correctly: return Task/Task<T>, await results, and let exceptions flow.
gotchas: async void swallows exceptions from the caller's point of view
Calling .Result or .Wait() blocks and can deadlock
Forgetting to await means the work may not have finished
goodSolutionShows: Task-returning signatures all the way up
shapeHints: loading a user profile then their settings
a fake HTTP client that returns after a delay

Intermediate.learningGoal: Run independent async work concurrently and support cancellation.
gotchas: Awaiting in a loop runs work sequentially when it could run concurrently
Task.WhenAll surfaces only the first exception when awaited
A CancellationToken that is accepted but never passed down or checked
goodSolutionShows: CancellationToken passed through to every async call
shapeHints: fetching several feeds at once with a timeout

Advanced.learningGoal: Build resilient async helpers: retries with backoff, throttled concurrency and timeouts.
gotchas: Retrying on cancellation instead of stopping
Timeouts implemented with Task.Delay that leave the original task running unobserved
goodSolutionShows: SemaphoreSlim or Parallel.ForEachAsync to cap concurrency
Retry loop that respects cancellation and only retries transient failures
Deterministic tests via an injected delay/clock abstraction

Expert.learningGoal: Understand ValueTask, IAsyncEnumerable and synchronization context subtleties.
gotchas: Awaiting a ValueTask twice is invalid
Forgetting [EnumeratorCancellation] on an async iterator's token
goodSolutionShows: IAsyncEnumerable with cancellation wired via WithCancellation
ValueTask used only on hot paths that often complete synchronously
Library code that doesn't depend on a captured context
shapeHints: a paged API client exposed as IAsyncEnumerable
a cache whose hit path returns ValueTask
